subject: Peregrine Labs - availability rider and notification flow
messages:
From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@peregrine.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@peregrine.com, Claire Boyd <claire.boyd@peregrine.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Availability rider & notification flow - initial ask

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to get a bit more specific on the availability commitments we need in the order form and an exhibit we can attach to the MSA. Two quick asks from our side: 

1) A rider that clarifies monthly uptime percentage, latency targets for our primary API route (/v1/generate), and the credit schedule if uptime misses the target.
2) A clear notification + escalation flow for operational incidents (pager, designated account manager, and backup contact) and expected timelines for responses and root-cause updates.

I've attached a short bullet list of our baseline requirements (Peregrine_SLA_Rider_v1.docx) — mainly conservative numbers because we run latency-sensitive batch scoring in production. Can your team confirm whether Redwood can: 
- Commit to a 99.9% monthly uptime objective for our dedicated model instance
- Offer a 95th percentile tail latency objective of <200ms for requests <=512 tokens
- Populate an order form clause tying credits to missed monthly uptime slabs (0.5% increments)

If some of that is not feasible, please propose the nearest alternative and call out optional mitigations (burst protection, reserved pre-warm capacity, regional failover). We hope to fold an exhibit into the MSA and then attach a signed order form.

Open to a quick 30-minute sync if that's easier.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Lee
Head of Platform Integrations
Peregrine Labs

Attachments: Peregrine_SLA_Rider_v1.docx
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@peregrine.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 22 Jul 2028 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Availability rider & notification flow - initial ask

Sam —

Thanks for the clear list and the attachment. Looping in Aditya (AE) and Monica (Procurement) to coordinate order-form language and the procurement path; Rishi from SRE will confirm feasibility and the latency objective.

High-level response now so you have something to share internally: 
- 99.9% monthly uptime for a dedicated instance is something we can design toward via dedicated pools + reserved capacity; we typically offer 99.95% on Dedicated for enterprise contracts but need to confirm the precise language in an exhibit.
- Tail latency (p95) <200ms for <=512 tokens is aggressive but plausible on certain GPU/instance types — depends on model/quantization and expected concurrency. Rishi, can you confirm viability and whether we should specify p95 vs p99?
- Credits schedule: we usually do tiered credits tied to percentage of monthly downtime; Monica will propose order-form wording that maps to your slabs.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Rishi to send a short ops note with achievable latency SLOs and any qualifiers.
2) Monica to draft a short exhibit and order-form clause we can iterate on.
3) I'll schedule a 30-min working session this week to align (Aditya will set the invite).

I'll also attach a draft order form from our side to start; it includes a placeholder availability exhibit and spaces for the regional fallback/backup contacts.

Kimberly Park
Senior Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Orderform_Draft_20280722.pdf
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, Sam Lee <sam.lee@peregrine.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 22 Jul 2028 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Availability rider & notification flow - initial ask

Sam / team —

Quick SRE note on latency & operational qualifiers: 
- For a dedicated pool with pinned GPUs (A100/Triton-optimized stacks) and sequence lengths <=512, p95 under 200ms is achievable at low to moderate concurrency. We recommend an explicit concurrency cap per instance in the exhibit (e.g., <=40 concurrent requests per node) to keep the guarantee enforceable.
- p99 targets are considerably more sensitive to burst patterns; if Peregrine needs p99 guarantees we should discuss a higher-tier provisioned/burst capacity add-on.
- For uptime: we can support a 99.9% monthly uptime SLA for Dedicated with an operational commitment to regional failover and a defined incident notification timeline: initial acknowledgement within 15 minutes for Sev1, detailed status within 60 minutes, and a root-cause summary within 72 hours.

Caveats: 
- Any customized guarantees will need an order-form exhibit referencing the exact model family/version and quantization profile.
- Credits calculation: our standard approach is crediting X% of monthly fees for each slab (we use 0.5% slabs in the draft). Monica, I'll attach a short Ops Appendix with recommended concurrency caps and the incident notification table for the exhibit.

Happy to review the Peregrine doc and mark it up.

Rishi Malhotra
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: (attached inline) SRE_Ops_Appendix_v1.pdf
From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@peregrine.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: Claire Boyd <claire.boyd@peregrine.com>, procurement@peregrine.com
Date: Tue, 24 Jul 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Availability rider & notification flow - initial ask

Kimberly —

Appreciate the quick responses. Claire from Legal and our procurement team reviewed the draft rider and attached our redlines (Peregrine_Redlines_v1.docx). High-level comments: 
- We accepted the 99.9% baseline but requested clearer phrasing for regional failover (we want explicit fallback to a secondary region within 15 minutes for critical paths).
- We pushed back on the concurrency cap language — prefer a performance-based credit instead of a hard concurrency cap (we can live with a defined scale-up/oversubscription penalty).
- We asked for an explicit list of contact roles in the notification flow (primary on-call, TAM, and an executive SLA owner) and to include escalation timelines for a multi-day incident.

Please review our redlines and let us know whether Redwood can accept the fallback/contacts edits or propose alternative language. If feasible, we'll drop the redline into our MSA SOW attachment and push for an approval this week.

If it's helpful, we can do a short call to walk the redlines — Claire and I are available Thursday morning.

Sam
Head of Platform Integrations
Peregrine Labs

Attachments: Peregrine_Redlines_v1.docx
